study.title: Acupuncture for Histamine-Induced Itch: Association With Increased Parasympathetic Tone and Connectivity of Putamen-Midcingulate Cortex
study.randomization: Session orders were determined with a random number table generated by Excel
study.blinding: Participants blinded to treatment condition; placebo-controlled; blinding assessed with Bang's blinding index
study.population: healthy volunteers between 18 and 50 years of age
study.disease_condition: experimentally induced histamine itch in healthy volunteers
study.inclusion_criteria: healthy participants between 18 and 50 years of age; no present history of asthma and atopic dermatitis; more than one experience with acupuncture
study.exclusion_criteria: skin problems on the stimulated site; antihistamine medications within 3 days before study; no itch response; long-term use of steroids; no flexible schedule; orthodontia; anxiety of acupuncture; MRI incompatibility

extraction_notes.note: The LF/HF ratio for non-responders at H3 is reported as '1127 (95% CI, 26.2–199.3)'. The point estimate of 1127 is internally inconsistent with the confidence interval of 26.2–199.3. This is likely a typographic or OCR error in the paper. The value was transcribed as reported.

Responder and non-responder subgroup n values in Study 2 fMRI analysis are not explicitly reported per subgroup; total n = 15 for neuroimaging. Subgroup sizes within fMRI analysis cannot be verified from the text.
Deqi sensation was not assessed or reported in this study. No deqi questionnaire or scale was administered.
Adverse events are not explicitly reported. The paper does not include an adverse event section or statement about safety outcomes.

The Table 1 lists seed regions as 'Putamen (l)', 'Putamen (r)', and 'Pallidum (l)'. The main reported finding involves the left putamen seed and pMCC cluster. Additional rows from Putamen (r) and Pallidum (l) seeds are also reported in Table 1 but are secondary findings. All rows were extracted.

The coordinate space (MNI) is inferred from the use of SPM12, CONN toolbox, and the Harvard-Oxford atlas, but is not explicitly stated as MNI in the results text. The atlas reference implies MNI space.

The putamen mask center MNI coordinates are reported as 'X = 26, Y = 3, Z = -1' in the methods text, but the atlas label states 'left putamen.' This internal inconsistency (positive X typically indicates right hemisphere in MNI) is present in the paper and was transcribed as reported.

The fMRI analysis focused on 'resting state scans (baseline) before acupuncture and induced 8-min resting state scans (itch).' The exact definition of which itch scan (H1: 0-4 min or H2: 4-8 min) was used as 'itch' for the main connectivity analysis is somewhat unclear from the text, though VAS at 8 min was used for correlation with connectivity.
STRICTA details are reported in Supplementary Appendix 1, which was not provided in the PDF. Some intervention details may be incomplete.

The study design involves a crossover where all 20 participants received both acupuncture and placebo, but the 'arm' structure is used here to represent both condition-level and responder/non-responder subgroup analyses. The responder/non-responder classification is based on itch response in the acupuncture condition only, not a separate randomized group.

Skin blood perfusion H4 values for acupuncture and placebo conditions separately are not explicitly stated in the text; only the p-value (p = 0.022) is given for H4 comparison. The mean values listed in the text (323.3, 391.5, 310.2 for acupuncture; 427.9, 587.1, 455.2 for placebo) correspond to H1, H2, H3 phases; H4 values are not separately reported in the text.

The paper does not report the T-statistic values for individual clusters in Table 1; only cluster size (in voxels) and FDR-corrected p-values are given. Statistic_value_exact was marked as not_reported for these rows.
